Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

tools.description: Retrieve up to three approved clauses for the current rule. Use when memory is enabled and model language would improve consistency.

tools.name: submit_finding
tools.description: Submit the final finding for this rule. After a successful call, stop calling tools.

paragraphs.text: 11.6 Content and Digital Certificates
Customer is solely responsible for:
a. all Content including, without limitation, its selection, licensing, accuracy, performance, maintenance, and support; and
b. the selection, management and use of any public and private keys and digital certificates it may use with the Services.
14.18 Data Protection

You agree to allow International Business Machines Corporation and entities within its Enterprise to store and use your contact information, including names, phone numbers, and e-mail addresses, anywhere they do business. Such information will be processed and used in connection with our business relationship, and may be provided to contractors, Business Partners, and assignees of IBM Corp. and entities within its Enterprise for uses consistent with their collective business activities, including communicating with you (for example, for processing orders, for promotions, and for marketing research). For personal information processed by IBM on your behalf as part of the Services, IBM will act in accordance with your instructions by following such processing and security obligations as are contained in this Agreement. You also confirm that you are solely responsible for ensuring that any processing and security obligations comply with applicable data protection laws. Your contact information shall not be considered personal information processed on your behalf.
14.2 Survival

Any of these terms and conditions which by their nature extend beyond the Agreement termination or expiration remain in effect until fulfilled, including, without limitation, Sections 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11.2, 11.3, 11.6, 12.2, 12.3, and 14, and apply to both Customer's and IBM's respective successors and assignees.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (rule IP).**

- **Where:** § 7.0 Materials (p0082–p0086). Deliverables default to **Type II Materials** — IBM or third parties hold all right, title and interest, and we get only a licence to use/reproduce/distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only," with no right to modify or sublicense (and "Enterprise" is limited to US entities).
- **Why it fails:** Preferred (we own work product created for us) is not met, and the fallback is also missed because the licence-back lacks modification and sublicensing rights and is territorially/entity-restricted.
- **Customer Data:** No assignment of our data to IBM (Content/Customer Components are defined as ours; IBM gets only Required Consents), but there is no express ownership statement — added for certainty, plus a no-joint-ownership sentence.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** flip the default to **Type I Materials** and insert a new § 7(e) confirming our ownership of Content/Customer Components and Type I Materials. Type I already grants IBM a broad licence back, so IBM retains use of its own know-how; fallback offered in the comment (keep Type II default if the licence is expanded to perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense).

ops.text: Insurance

IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000, covering IBM's handling of Content and of personal information processed by IBM on Customer's behalf; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

input.quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, committed volume, take-or-pay obligation or shortfall charge on Bluefly. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "volume" and "purchase" return nothing of that character: § 4.1 prices Charges only for Services actually ordered under Service Option Attachments/Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), § 11.5 addresses capacity planning rather than committed capacity, and § 12.3 confirms no goods are purchased. Bluefly also has a monthly termination-for-convenience right on one month's notice (§ 3.4) plus a no-charge exit if IBM changes the Services (§ 13.1), so there is no locked-in multi-year spend. This meets the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only). Two points to note but not redline: § 3.4(b) preserves "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments", and § 3.2 auto-renews each Service Option Attachment for a like term absent 90 days' notice — the attachments should be checked to confirm they contain no minimum-volume or take-or-pay pricing, which would be assessed under this rule when available.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "volume" and "purchase" return nothing of that character: § 4.1 prices Charges only for Services actually ordered under Service Option Attachments/Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), § 11.5 addresses capacity planning rather than committed capacity, and § 12.3 confirms no goods are purchased. Bluefly also has a monthly termination-for-convenience right on one month's notice (§ 3.4) plus a no-charge exit if IBM changes the Services (§ 13.1), so there is no locked-in multi-year spend. This meets the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only). content.text:
**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY)** — submitted.

- **What the document has:** § 5.1 warrants Services performed with "reasonable care and skill" using qualified personnel, plus a covenant to comply with laws applicable to IBM's business. § 5.2 makes those the exclusive warranties.
- **What is missing:** no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period, no no-malicious-code warranty, and no remedy (repair/replace/re-perform/refund). § 5.4(c) affirmatively puts all Materials on an unqualified "AS IS" footing, and §§ 5.4(a)–(b) disclaim error-free operation, capacity and performance. Support in §§ 11.1/12.2 is discretionary ("as reasonably determined by IBM"), so it is not a substitute remedy.
- **Why deviation, not fallback:** the fallback still requires a conformance warranty (90 days software / 30 days services) with real remedies; neither element exists, so the clause fails on material terms while stopping just short of full walk-away AS IS.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new § 5.1(c) adding a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty with a re-perform/repair/replace/refund remedy, plus an "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1" carve-out at the head of § 5.4(c) so the disclaimer no longer swallows the express warranty.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Base Terms contain no minimum purchase commitment, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic binding Bluefly:

- **§ 4.1 Charges** — Charges are only for Services specified in Service Option Attachments/Order Forms and may be one-time, installment, recurring or usage-based; nothing establishes a floor. This satisfies the **preferred** position (fees for usage or ordered services only).

- **§ 12.3** — no goods are sold or leased, so no purchase quantity obligation.
- **§ 3.4** — Bluefly may terminate for convenience at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice, and **§ 13.1** gives a no-charge exit on IBM service changes, so there is no multi-year lock-in.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: § 3.4(b) preserves "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments," and § 3.2 auto-renews each Service Option Attachment absent 90 days' notice. The attachments should be reviewed to confirm they carry no minimum-volume or take-or-pay pricing; if they do, this rule would be re-assessed against those documents.

ops.text: Insurance

IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000, covering IBM's handling of Content and of personal information processed by IBM on Customer's behalf; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement currently addresses only accrued payment obligations on termination, with no right to transition assistance or return of our Content. We have added our standard exit provision: up to six months' transition assistance at IBM's then-current rates, return of Content in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. We can work with 90 days of transition assistance if six months is an issue.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Content and other Customer data in its possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Content and Customer data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

The Agreement therefore fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export) and leaves us exposed to loss of Content on termination. You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
input.rationale:
The Agreement contains no insurance clause anywhere: a full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the section outline has no insurance heading. The nearest ri[REDACTED] provisions (§ 14.12 Risk of Loss, § 5.3 Security) address allocation of loss and security features but impose no obligation on IBM to carry coverage.

IBM is squarely within the rule's scope: it operates the e-business Hosting Environment, holds "Content" (defined at p0017 as the information, software and data Customer provides), and under § 14.18 processes personal information on Customer's behalf. A hosting vendor that processes personal data with no insurance at all is the rule's walk-away scenario, not merely a shortfall against the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M), so this is a "missing" finding requiring insertion.

Redline inserts a new § 14.12A adjacent to Risk of Loss at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request. I used the document's own defined term "Content" plus the § 14.18 personal-information language rather than the playbook's "Customer Data", which is not a defined term in this agreement. The obligation runs against IBM only and does not create any burden on our party. The comment offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as a landing zone. Severity is low.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 14.12A requiring IBM to maintain CGL, professional liability (E&O) and cyber liability insurance, with certificates on request.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM hosts our environment and processes our Content and personal information, but the Agreement contains no insurance requirement, so we have added a standard provision (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request). If helpful, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000, covering IBM's handling of Content and of personal information processed by IBM on Customer's behalf; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.
Insurance

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.rationale:
The Agreement contains no insurance clause anywhere: a full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the section outline has no insurance heading. The nearest ri[REDACTED] provisions (§ 14.12 Risk of Loss, § 5.3 Security) address allocation of loss and security features but impose no obligation on IBM to carry coverage.

IBM is squarely within the rule's scope: it operates the e-business Hosting Environment, holds "Content" (defined at p0017 as the information, software and data Customer provides), and under § 14.18 processes personal information on Customer's behalf. A hosting vendor that processes personal data with no insurance at all is the rule's walk-away scenario, not merely a shortfall against the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M), so this is a "missing" finding requiring insertion.

Redline inserts a new § 14.12A adjacent to Risk of Loss at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request. I used the document's own defined term "Content" plus the § 14.18 personal-information language rather than the playbook's "Customer Data", which is not a defined term in this agreement. The obligation runs against IBM only and does not create any burden on our party. The comment offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as a landing zone. Severity is low.

content.text:
**Finding: MISSING** (confidence 0.9)

The agreement has no exit provision at all. § 3.5 "Effect of Termination" covers only accrued payment obligations, and document-wide searches for *transition*, *return*, *export*, *delete/destroy* and *migrate* returned no hits. The nearby candidates don't help: § 11.6 makes us solely responsible for our own Content, § 14.18 covers only contact-information processing, and § 14.2 simply lists 3.5 among surviving terms — surviving a clause that says nothing about data return.

Because IBM hosts our Content, this falls short of even the fallback position (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export) and edges toward walk-away territory, since nothing obliges IBM to give our data back on exit.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** inserted a new paragraph after p0049 in § 3.5 at the preferred position — (a) up to six months' transition assistance at IBM's then-current rates on request, (b) return/export of all Content and Customer data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and (c) deletion thereafter with written certification. The clause is drafted to cover termination of the Agreement or any individual Service Option Attachment, matching the document's structure, and the 90-day fallback is offered in the comment.

**Finding: MISSING** (severity low, confidence 0.90)

**What I found**

There is no insurance clause anywhere in this agreement. A full-text search for "insurance" returned zero results, and the 51-section outline contains no insurance heading. The two nearest neighbours flagged by the planner both turned out to be non-substitutes:

- **§ 14.12 Risk of Loss** allocates risk of loss between the parties but requires no coverage.
- **§ 5.3 Security** actually runs the other way — it disclaims IBM's warranty of secure operation and states IBM "does not warrant secure operation of the Services."

**Why the rule applies**

IBM is squarely a services/hosting vendor touching our data:
- It operates the e-business Hosting Environment and holds "Content," defined at p0017 as the information, software and data Customer provides.
- Under § 14.18, IBM processes personal information on our behalf.

A hosting vendor processing personal data with no insurance at all is the rule's **walk-away** scenario, not a shortfall against the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). That makes insertion appropriate rather than a rationale-only note.

**Redline**

New § 14.12A, placed adjacent to Risk of Loss, at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request.

Two drafting judgments worth flagging:

1. **Defined-term substitution.** The playbook's model language uses "Customer Data," which I confirmed is *not* defined in this agreement (`get_definition` returned not-found, nearest match "Customer"). Inserting it would have created an undefined term. I instead used the document's own defined term "Content" plus the § 14.18 personal-information formulation, so the clause hooks into existing definitions.

2. **Op ordering.** My first validated proposal listed the heading before the body, but both ops insert after the same paragraph — depending on how the tool applies same-anchor inserts, the body could have landed above its own heading. I reversed the order and re-validated to guarantee the heading renders first.

The obligation runs against IBM only and imposes nothing on Bluefly. The comment offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as a landing zone.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Base Terms — 18 rules assessed 

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Eight clauses are compliant (several better than our preferred position), eight are deviations requiring redline, and two rules have no usable clause at all.

The commercial shape of the deal is broadly acceptable: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-purchase commitment, non-solicit or audit right imposed on us; governing law is New York with no arbitration; and the Vendor-side IP indemnity in § 8.1 sits at our fallback with indemnification payments carved out of the cap.

The problems cluster in three areas. First, **IP and licence**: § 7.0 defaults all deliverables to Type II (IBM-owned) Materials with a narrow intra-Enterprise licence back, and the § 12.1 Base Components licence is expressly *revocable* and runs to Customer only — no Affiliates or contractors. Second, **liability and warranty**: the caps in §§ 9.1/9.2 are mutual and on an acceptable basis, but carve-outs for confidentiality/data, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement are absent, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM liability for loss of our records or data outright; § 5.1 offers only a workmanlike-standard warranty which § 5.4(c) then swallows with an unqualified "AS IS". Third, **exit**: our § 3.4 convenience right is conditioned on uncapped early termination charges defined outside this document, § 3.2 auto-renews for a term equal to the previous term on 90 days' notice with no uplift cap, and there is no transition assistance, Content return or deletion obligation anywhere. There is also no insurance clause of any kind, despite IBM hosting our Content and processing personal information under § 14.18.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | At fallback; indemnity payments carved out of the cap under § 9.1(a). Preferred non-IP heads absent (noted only). |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (§ 7.0 Materials) | Type II default gives IBM title; licence back excludes modification/sublicensing and is limited to our Enterprise. Flip default to Type I and confirm Content ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Caps mutual and acceptable, but no carve-outs for confidentiality/data, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP; § 9.1(c)(2) excludes data/records liability. Add mutual § 9.3 carve-outs. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.10 Assignment | One-sided: consent gate binds us only, IBM assignment unrestricted. Make mutual, add competitor bar and affiliate/asset-sale carve-out. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity or requirements obligation; § 14.16 preserves freedom to contract with others. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Early termination charges set in Attachment A, uncapped and not reproduced here. Cap at three months' charges and make sole remedy. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 12.1 License | Grant is "revocable" with no cause standard and excludes Affiliates and contractors; § 14.17 forecloses implied extension. Remove revocability at will and extend scope. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant; § 14.11 No Resale is an ordinary redistribution limit. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | One month's notice and no IBM convenience right meet preferred position, but uncapped exit charges (§ 3.4(b)) and no refund of prepaid Charges (§ 3.5) fail the fallback. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No audit, inspection or system-access right; better than preferred. § 11.3 cooperation duty noted only. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law, no arbitration. Silence on exclusive venue is a sub-element, noted not redlined. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No MFN obligation on us; § 14.16 confirms the opposite. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | Charges for ordered Services only; monthly exit right. Attachments to be checked for take-or-pay pricing. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel | No no-hire or non-solicit covenant. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 3.2 Renewal | Renews for a term equal to the previous term, 90 days' notice, no uplift cap or reminder. Move to 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, reminder and CPI/3% cap. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | No transition, Content return, export or deletion language anywhere. Insert six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion (90-day fallback available). |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Workmanlike standard only; no conformance or no-malicious-code warranty, no period, no remedy, and § 5.4(c) puts Materials "AS IS". Add 90-day warranty with remedy and carve out of the disclaimer. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance obligation at all despite IBM hosting Content and processing personal information (§ 14.18). Insert § 14.12A (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp, certificates). |

---

## Walk-away items

These three points fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature, not trading chips:

1. **§ 12.1 licence revocable at IBM's discretion, Customer-only (LICENSE).** A revocable-at-will grant with no Affiliate or contractor coverage, reinforced by § 14.17, is not a usable licence. Minimum acceptable outcome: revocation limited to our uncured material breach, with Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf covered.
2. **§ 3.2 auto-renewal for a term equal to the previous term (RENEWAL).** A multi-year initial term that rolls into a further multi-year term on 90 days' notice, with no cap on renewal Charge increases, is walk-away territory. Minimum acceptable outcome: 12-month renewals with a 30-day opt-out (60 days with a 5% uplift cap is the fallback landing zone).
3. **No insurance whatsoever (INSURANCE).** IBM hosts our Content and processes personal information on our behalf under § 14.18; a hosting vendor with no coverage at all is the rule's walk-away scenario rather than a shortfall. Fallback landing zone: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

We also flag, short of walk-away, that the combination of uncapped Attachment A early termination charges (§ 3.4(b)) and the absence of any transition or data-return obligation (§ 3.5) can make our convenience right economically illusory and leave our Content stranded. These should be resolved together.

---

## Next steps

1. **Obtain the missing documents before we finalise our position.** Attachment A and each Service Option Attachment drive the early termination charges (§ 3.4(b)) and would also be where any minimum-volume or take-or-pay pricing sits. We cannot close out LD, T4C or MINCOMMIT without them.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations and two missing clauses: Type I Materials default plus a Content ownership statement; a new mutual § 9.3 carve-out provision leaving the existing caps intact; mutual assignment in § 14.10; a three-month cap and sole-remedy wording on early termination charges plus pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges; § 12.1 licence scope and revocability; § 3.2 renewal mechanics; a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty carved out of § 5.4(c); § 3.5 transition, return and certified deletion; and new § 14.12A insurance.
3. **Sequence the negotiation** around the three walk-away items first (licence scope, renewal, insurance), then the critical IP and liability carve-out points, then the exit economics package. Where we have identified a fallback (renewal at 60 days/5%; transition at 90 days plus 30-day export; insurance at E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M; early termination charges capped at three months), we have authority to land there.
4. **Confirm we do not reopen the compliant clauses.** The eight compliant findings — including the § 8.1 indemnity at fallback and the absence of audit, exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment and non-solicit obligations — are at or better than our position and should be left alone.
5. **Record the noted-only items** (venue silence in § 14.3, absence of preferred non-IP indemnity heads, the § 11.3 information-provision duty, late payment fees under § 4.2) in the deal file so they are not raised as issues in this round."}
